Before you choose a plan

Support that stays
manageable.

Care is optional. It is also separate from the original website project and from third-party bills.

  • Included tasks and content-change allowances are written down.
  • Plan costs, billing and cancellation terms are agreed before starting.
  • New features, redesigns and extra pages need a separate scope.
  • Advertising, SEO campaigns and third-party charges are not included unless expressly agreed.
  • Unlimited changes and round-the-clock support are not part of the offer.

A little more clarity

Care should feel
straightforward.

Do I have to choose a care plan?

No. Website care is optional. We explain the maintenance and ownership responsibilities at handover so you can decide how you want the site looked after.

Can you look after a site you did not build?

We would first need to review the platform, access, existing condition and responsibilities. A review does not automatically mean a care plan is available; the work and suitability need to be agreed.

What happens if I need a larger change?

We discuss the request, check it against your plan and explain any additional scope or cost before proceeding. New pages, features or redesigns are treated as separate work unless the agreement includes them.

How are backups and incidents handled?

The plan identifies the responsible provider, backup arrangements and recovery process, plus the support route for an incident. These depend on the website and hosting setup; there is no blanket promise of uninterrupted service or guaranteed recovery.

What do you need to assess my website?

A website address, the platform if you know it, and a short description of the help you need are a useful start. Do not include passwords or sensitive customer information in a project brief.
